metadata.title: A Covariant Screened Theory for a Dark-Energy-Tied Galaxy Law: a Khronon Parent with One Stiffness Term, Healthy in Its Literal Form, Clean in the Solar System, with Fitted Constants and Pending Cosmology (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-22). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

The owner's programme studies a gravity framework whose galactic law is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE), kappa = 1/2 fitted; its extra gravitating mass is a collisionless 'cold energy' medium, not a particle. The companion note PAPER58 found that only a screened version, with a stiffness length L*, passes both Cassini and the galactic law. This note writes that screened theory covariantly and tests it; criteria were frozen before computing, mutation controls run, both a0 footings reported and never pooled.

(1) The action: the Blanchet-Skordis Khronon theory in its literal form (beta = 0, eta = 0, Blanchet-Skordis K(Q) dust) plus an independent spatial covector P and one stiffness term -(gamma_L/2)(D.P)^2. Its static limit is AQUAL with mu = x/(1+x) exactly; the free function that gives this lies outside Blanchet and Skordis's admissible class (postulated), as is the stiffness term. AeST reproduces everything except the stiffness term, which is identically zero there; the record's earlier action is this theory with eta > 0, which is ill-posed. (2) Health: no ghost or gradient instability on the backgrounds tested; only the two tensor modes propagate, at c. The instantaneous leaf sector is the Euler-Lagrange system of a strictly convex functional, hence well posed in the weak field; it violates 'no influence faster than light' by a real signal of about 1e-46 m/s^2 and meets the single-global-time criterion. (3) Tests: galaxies follow the law; Cassini passes in all 24 cells by 4.8e7 to 5.1e9 (the frozen rule reads UNDECIDED on one float-cancellation check); planets at most 0.17 of a bound; outer globulars exclude the unscreened law in all 18 cells and give a lower bound on L* (21.68 / 22.85 pc) but no finite L* beats Newton; binary pulsars and GW170817 do not constrain it; dwarf satellites show a +0.89 dex gap whose supply is only conditionally met; ALMA is expected unscorable. (4) kappa, L* and the dust abundance are fitted, not derived. (5) Pending: the native CMB (a patched Boltzmann code is validated, no native spectrum run; it can test only the dust sector and the cosmological G ratio, since a0 is absent at linear order) and the native cosmic-shear run (running, no verdict). Gaia DR4 is the sealed decisive test: screened gamma_v - 1 = 8.1e-6 against about 1.17 for the unscreened reading.

Companion notes: PAPER58 v1.1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23579379), PAPER57 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23532885), PAPER49 v1.2 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23533323). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).
